learning_outcomes.text: The graduate has knowledge related to programming, mathematics, engineering and technology and has the skills to use them to create complex information technology systems.
The graduate has adequate knowledge related to the use of integrated development environments for creating large complex applications.
The graduate has the ability to observe and obtain information from various sources.
The graduate has the ability to develop, design and create new applications, systems or products using best practices of the field.
The graduate has the necessary skills for computer program design and software systems analysis.
The graduate has the necessary skills to develop GUI applications using architectural templates suitable for a specific user interaction applications.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to virtual environments, input/output devices, state of the art
Virtual object modeling (geometric primitives, custom build geometries)
Position and orientation representation (position vector, Euler angles, orientation matrix)
Scene graph (reference frames, node hierarchy, node types, light nodes, fog)
Scene optimizations (level of details, textures, cell-segmentation)
Simulating spatial phenomena (fog, smoke, fire, fluids)
teaching_methods: Exposition: presentation, explanations, practical examples, demonstrations, case-study discussions
assessment_rules: The final grade requires a minimum of 5. The final grade is calculated based on project evaluation (40%) and semester project/lab activity evaluation (50%).
